title: Operator Tenant Cutover Validation Checklist — Private Deploys (2026)
author: Rahul Gupta
content:
Summary:
This checklist is an operator-facing, preflight and validation playbook for tenant cutovers (traffic switch) during Private / VPC deployments. It is intended for on-call operators, field engineering, and release engineers responsible for migrating production traffic to a new tenant instance, model variant, or region. The goal is to provide deterministic validation gates, quick rollback triggers, and evidence capture for post-cutover review.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: Operators, Field Engineers, SREs.
- Scope: Tenant-level cutover where live traffic is switched from a staging/blue instance to a target/green instance inside a Private/VPC deployment. This checklist assumes the target instance has passed standard acceptance tests and that the control-plane handshake and KMS bindings are complete. Does NOT replace full change-control templates.

Before you begin (preflight verification)
- Confirm approvals and runbook: change ticket ID, customer contact, maintenance window, and approval signatures.
- Verify operator access: ssh key or bastion access, kube / operator RBAC, and temporary escalation contacts.
- Snapshot evidence: take pre-cutover telemetry snapshot (see Evidence collection).

Preflight quick-checks (operator)
1) Customer and network
   - Confirm customer IAM mapping and tenant service account bound to KMS/HSM.
   - Validate VPC routing & NACLs: control-plane and data-plane CIDR reachability in both directions.
   - Validate egress ACLs for telemetry collector endpoints.

2) Capacity and runtime
   - Verify GPU node pool health: node status == Ready and unschedulable == false.
   - Check model artifact checksum and quantization profile id.
   - Confirm KV-cache warmup targets: prefix cache hit rate >= 80% (see thresholds).

3) Observability and SLOs
   - Ensure metrics ingestion is healthy: per-tenant metrics freshness <= 60s.
   - Confirm tracing is enabled for new tenant path (sample rate 1/50).
   - Verify alerting is muted/unmuted as appropriate: alert throttle for cutover window set to operator channel.

Preflight commands (examples)
- K8s node health:
  kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu --no-headers | awk '{print $2}'

- Model artifact checksum:
  shasum -a 256 /srv/models/<model>-v<ver>.tar.gz

- KV cache stats (admin API):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://runtime-admin.internal/v1/tenants/$TENANT/cache/status" | jq

Cutover validation gates (ordered)
These gates are small, deterministic checks that must pass before moving to the next stage. If any gate fails, follow the Rollback and Throttle rules.

Gate A — Smoke traffic mirror (10 minutes)
- Objective: Mirror 1-5% of live traffic from prod -> target to validate request path and runtime behaviors without impacting customers.
- Success criteria (10 min window):
  - 200 OK ratio for mirrored requests >= 99.5%
  - Latency p95 of mirrored requests <= +50ms of baseline
  - Model output shape / schema validation == pass (structured output checks)

Gate B — Gradual traffic ramp (30 minutes)
- Objective: Move traffic in increments (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with soak/observation periods and automated rollback triggers.
- At each increment verify:
  - Error rate (5xx) delta <= +0.1 percentage points vs baseline for the tenant
  - Token-per-request cost delta <= +10% (billing proxy snapshot)
  - End-to-end p95 latency delta <= +15% or <= +200ms absolute (whichever is lower)

Gate C — Functional evals (post-50% soak)
- Run canned evaluation prompt set (20 prompts) against the new instance. Required pass: at least 18/20 prompts match baseline acceptance criteria (semantic similarity thresholds and hallucination checks).

Rollback and throttle rules
- Immediate rollback triggers (abort and revert to prior routing):
  - sustained increase in 5xx rate > 1% absolute for 5 minutes
  - p95 latency exceeds baseline by 300ms for 90% of requests in a 5-minute window
  - KV cache consistency errors (stale cache hits, invalid keys) observed
- Throttle (slow rollout) conditions: any transient, non-deterministic deviation where operator discretion is required (e.g., small latency blips, minor cost delta).
- Rollback procedure (high level):
  1. Halt further ramping, set traffic to 0% for target via routing API.
  2. Switch traffic back to incumbent instance and verify traffic stabilization.
  3. Capture full evidence bundle (see Evidence).
  4. Open incident with classification: cutover-regression and notify customer + success team.

Post-cutover validation (immediately after 100% traffic)
- Verify post-cutover telemetry: per-tenant metrics fresh, no new alerts, request volume matches expected.
- Run 100 user-simulated transactions from the customer’s representative region and confirm agreement with baseline responses (automated script).
- Confirm billing records show expected token accounting for first 60 minutes.

Evidence collection (mandatory)
- Pre-cutover: control-plane logs, node snapshots, model artifact checksum, admin API cache snapshot.
- During cutover: traffic mirror logs, ramp increments timestamps, feature-flag states, sample traces for failed requests.
- Post-cutover: final model hash, metric window export (CSV), and the canned eval results.
- Storage: Upload evidence tarball to S3 path: s3://redwood-cutover-evidence/<customer>/<change-id>/<timestamp>.tar.gz

Operator checklists and templates (copy & use)
- Change ticket template: [CHANGE-ID] TenantCutover — Customer: <org> — Window: <start/end>
- Rollback reason codes (use when filing incident): kernel-timeout, model-mismatch, cache-inconsistency, networking-rtx, capacity-exhaustion

Safety knobs and automated mitigations
- Canary scoring service: automatic canary fail if composite score < 0.92 (score components: success-rate, latency-normalized, fidelity-evals).
- Circuit breaker: per-tenant request-rate circuit with open threshold at 2x baseline sustained for 30s.
- Emergency kill: operator API to immediately divert traffic and set flows to read-only for writes that cause inconsistent state.

Cutover checklist table (operators should tick each row)
| Item | Good state / Threshold | Command / Evidence | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Customer IAM bound | SA bound to KMS, last bind <= 24h | adminctl iam status $TENANT | Platform-OPS |
| Node pool health | Ready nodes >= required-capacity | kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu | Field-Eng |
| KV cache warm | hit_rate >= 80% | curl admin/cache/status | Runtime-Team |
| Mirrored 10m smoke | 200 OK >= 99.5% | capture mirror logs | Oncall |
| Eval prompts pass | >= 90% acceptance | /scripts/eval-run.sh | Applied-ML |
| Billing sanity | token delta within 10% | billing/proxy/snapshot | Fin-Ops |

Operator run commands (quick reference)
- Mirror traffic (routing API):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" "https://router.internal/v1/tenants/$TENANT/mirror" -d '{"target":"tenants/$TENANT/green","rate_pct":5}'

- Ramp traffic (routing API):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" "https://router.internal/v1/tenants/$TENANT/route" -d '{"target":"green","percent":25}'

- Capture evidence bundle:
  tar czf /tmp/evidence-$TENANT-$CHANGEID.tar.gz /var/log/runtime /tmp/eval-results.json && aws s3 cp /tmp/evidence-$TENANT-$CHANGEID.tar.gz s3://redwood-cutover-evidence/$TENANT/$CHANGEID/

Common failure modes and operator remediation tips
- Slow model startup (symptom): high cold-start tail latency. Remediation: increase warm replica count, pre-warm KV prefixes, and re-run smoke mirror.
- Cache desync (symptom): request responses contain stale tokens or incorrect persona. Remediation: flush prefix, rehydrate from snapshot, pause ramp until cache stabilizes.
- Network MTU or packet loss (symptom): sporadic retries and elevated latency. Remediation: validate VPC MTU, BFD/keepalive settings, and route propagation.

Post-incident review (template)
- Timeline: record timestamps for: preflight complete, mirror start, each ramp step, rollback if any, final stabilization.
- Metrics windows: include 5-min windows before/during/after for request rate, p95 latency, 5xx rate, and cache hit rate.
- Root cause hypothesis and corrective actions: one-line summary, owner and target date.

Appendix: thresholds and definitions
- Baseline: last 24h tenant rolling median for metric X (unless otherwise specified).
- Acceptance: semantic-fidelity threshold = cosine sim >= 0.82 on eval embedding comparator.
- Evidence retention: cutover artifacts must be retained for 180 days.

If you are uncertain at any step, pause and escalate to the on-call Field Engineer and Applied ML contact.
